slides.title: 5 tricks used to market “research peptides”
slides.text: Spot the marketing, not the deal 👉

slides.title: “Research only” + health promises
slides.text: The label says not for human use, while the ads promise healing, fat loss or anti-aging. Both can't be true.

slides.title: A certificate that proves little
slides.text: A generic certificate of analysis, not tied to a batch or a named lab, is used as a stamp of quality.

slides.title: “Pharmaceutical grade” with no approval
slides.text: Sounds official, but no medicines agency has approved the product. Independent tests of market products have found less substance than labeled, or impurities.

list: Testimonials and before/after photos instead of studies
“Same as the prescription drug, just cheaper”

slides.text: No marketing trick makes an unapproved substance safe.

caption:
5 tricks used to market “research peptides” 🚩 Health promises on a “not for human use” product, certificates that prove little, “pharmaceutical grade” with no approval.
